questions.stem: The total coastline of India, including the coastline of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep, is approximately:

options.option_text: 7,517 km (mainland ~5,423 km + island territories)
6,100 km (mainland only, islands excluded)
8,900 km (including estuarine and tidal creeks)
5,000 km (as per the 1961 Survey of India measurement)

questions.explanation: INDIA'S TOTAL COASTLINE = 7,516.6 km (commonly rounded to 7,517 km). Breakdown: MAINLAND coastline = 5,422.6 km (9 coastal states + 4 UTs). ISLAND COASTLINE = A&N Islands (~1,962 km) + Lakshadweep (~132 km). India has the 18th longest coastline in the world. COASTAL STATES (9): Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala (west coast) + Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal (east coast). COASTAL UTs (4): Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli (west), Puducherry (east/west), Lakshadweep, A&N Islands. UPSC ANGLE: The Supreme Court's 2011 judgment on coastal regulation zones (CRZ) used the 'mainland coastline' figure for calculating buffer zones. EXAM TRAP: 6,100 km refers to mainland-only (older figures used in some textbooks); 7,517 km is the official comprehensive figure. PYQ FREQUENCY: appears every 2-3 cycles in SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims geography; RRB NTPC regularly tests this.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Eastern Coastal Plain from the Western Coastal Plain of India?

options.option_text: Eastern coast is wider with well-developed deltas; western coast is narrow with lagoons and backwaters
Eastern coast is narrow with lagoons; western coast is wider with large river deltas
Both coasts are similar in width; eastern receives more rainfall due to Bay of Bengal
Western coast has better natural harbours because of shallow continental shelf (not this)

questions.explanation: EASTERN COASTAL PLAIN: wider (100-120 km), formed by large deltas of Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri — called 'Delta Coast'. Has sandy beaches, fertile soil. Natural harbours rare because of shallow, straight coast. WESTERN COASTAL PLAIN: narrow (10-25 km), formed by the Western Ghats running close to the coast. No major river deltas — rivers are short and fast. Rich in LAGOONS and BACKWATERS (Kerala's famous backwaters). Has rocky headlands, deep water close to shore → BETTER NATURAL HARBOURS. HARBOUR PARADOX: Western coast has better natural harbours despite being narrower — because deep water near shore allows large ships. Eastern coast needs artificial ports (Visakhapatnam was a natural harbour exception). CONTINENTAL SHELF: Eastern coast has a WIDER and shallower continental shelf (better for fishing, oil exploration). Western coast has a NARROW, steep continental shelf. PYQ FREQUENCY: east vs west coast distinction is a perennial SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims, RRB NTPC topic. EXAM TRAP: Option D reverses the harbour logic — shallow shelf = bad harbours, not good ones.

questions.stem: The Konkan, Malabar, and Coromandel are names of coastal stretches in India. Which of the following correctly maps each name to its location?

options.option_text: Konkan = Maharashtra-Goa coast; Malabar = Kerala-Karnataka coast; Coromandel = Tamil Nadu-Andhra coast
Konkan = Gujarat coast; Malabar = Maharashtra coast; Coromandel = Odisha coast (not this)
Konkan = Kerala coast; Malabar = Tamil Nadu coast; Coromandel = West Bengal coast
Konkan = Goa-Karnataka coast; Malabar = Gujarat coast; Coromandel = Andhra-Odisha coast

questions.explanation: NAMED COASTAL STRETCHES of India — West Coast (south to north): MALABAR COAST = Kerala + southern Karnataka (Kasaragod to Mangalore region); famous for spice trade, backwaters, Portuguese era. KONKAN COAST = Goa + Maharashtra coastline (Goa to Mumbai-Ratnagiri-Raigad); steep, rocky, narrow. Beyond Konkan northward = KATHIAWAR/KUTCH coast (Gujarat). East Coast (north to south): COROMANDEL COAST = Tamil Nadu + southern Andhra Pradesh (Pondicherry to Mahabalipuram region); sandy, no good harbours, deltaic. North of Coromandel = NORTHERN CIRCARS coast (Andhra + Odisha). UPSC ANGLE: Malabar Coast featured in Vasco da Gama's landing at Calicut (1498) — crucial for colonial history. Coromandel Coast was the base for British East India Company's early settlements (Madras/Fort St. George 1639). PYQ FREQUENCY: coastal names appear in SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims, TNPSC, KPSC regularly. MEMORY AID: going anti-clockwise from Kerala: M-K-K (Malabar-Konkan-Kutch on west); C-NC on east (Coromandel-Northern Circars).

questions.stem: India's longest coastline among all states belongs to which state?

options.option_text: Gujarat (~1,600 km — due to the irregular Rann and Gulf of Kutch coastline)
Andhra Pradesh (~975 km — longest on the eastern coast) (not this)
Tamil Nadu (~1,076 km — including Gulf of Mannar) (not this)
Maharashtra (~720 km — longest on the Konkan coast) (not this)

questions.explanation: GUJARAT has India's longest state coastline at approximately 1,600 km — this is because of the highly irregular, indented nature of its coast including the Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay), the Rann of Kutch, and numerous creeks and inlets. RANKING: Gujarat (~1,600 km) > Andhra Pradesh (~975 km) > Tamil Nadu (~1,076 km — note: some surveys place TN above AP) > Maharashtra (~720 km). Gujarat's coastline peculiarity: it is on the WESTERN coast but curves so much that it is longer than any eastern state. Also has the Kandla Port (now Deendayal Port) — one of India's major ports. UPSC ANGLE: Gujarat's long coastline is a key factor in its economic geography — Mundra Port (largest private port), Hazira LNG terminal, GIFT City proximity. PYQ FREQUENCY: longest coastline state appears nearly every year in SSC CGL, IBPS PO GA, RRB NTPC. EXAM TRAP: Tamil Nadu vs Andhra Pradesh ranking is close and sometimes debated — but Gujarat's top rank is unambiguous.

questions.stem: The Sagarmala Programme, launched to modernise India's port-led development, is administered by which ministry?

options.option_text: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (formerly Shipping)
Ministry of Commerce and Industry (since ports drive exports)
Ministry of External Affairs (since ports are international gateways)
Ministry of Finance (since port infrastructure involves large capital outlay)

questions.explanation: SAGARMALA PROGRAMME — launched in 2015, administered by the MINISTRY OF PORTS, SHIPPING AND WATERWAYS. Four pillars: (1) PORT MODERNISATION — upgrading major and non-major ports. (2) PORT-LED INDUSTRIALISATION — setting up coastal economic zones (CEZ). (3) COASTAL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT — skilling coastal fishermen and communities. (4) IMPROVING PORT CONNECTIVITY — rail, road, inland waterways linkages. KEY TARGETS: reduce logistics cost, boost coastal shipping and inland waterways, develop 'Blue Economy.' The ministry was renamed from 'Ministry of Shipping' to 'Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways' in 2021 to reflect expanded mandate. UPSC ANGLE: Sagarmala connects to India's Blue Economy policy — 95% of India's trade by volume and 68% by value moves via sea. The programme identifies 600+ projects worth ₹6 lakh crore. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sagarmala appears in UPSC Prelims GS-3 (infrastructure), SSC CGL GA, IBPS PO. EXAM TRAP: the ministry name changed — older MCQs say 'Shipping'; current answer is 'Ports, Shipping and Waterways'.

questions.stem: India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to how many nautical miles from the baseline, granting India sovereign rights over marine resources in that zone?

options.option_text: 200 nautical miles (as per UNCLOS 1982)
12 nautical miles (territorial sea limit, not EEZ)
350 nautical miles (extended continental shelf limit)
100 nautical miles (contiguous zone double)

questions.explanation: EXCLUSIVE ECONOMIC ZONE (EEZ) = 200 NAUTICAL MILES from the baseline (low-water line along the coast). Defined by UNCLOS (UN Convention on the Law of the Sea), 1982, which India ratified in 1995. MARITIME ZONE LAYERS: (1) INTERNAL WATERS — landward of baseline, full sovereignty. (2) TERRITORIAL SEA — up to 12 nm; full sovereignty, foreign ships have 'innocent passage.' (3) CONTIGUOUS ZONE — 12-24 nm; India can enforce customs, immigration, sanitation laws. (4) EEZ — 12-200 nm; sovereign rights (NOT full sovereignty) over exploration and exploitation of natural resources — fish, oil, minerals, energy. (5) CONTINENTAL SHELF — up to 350 nm in some cases; rights over seabed resources. India's EEZ = ~2.37 million sq km. UPSC ANGLE: India has submitted claims to the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) for extended continental shelf beyond 200 nm in the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean. PYQ FREQUENCY: EEZ = 200 nm is tested every exam cycle — UPSC, SSC CGL, NDA, CAPF.

questions.stem: The Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Vembanad Lake (Kerala) are both lagoons on India's coast. What distinguishes a lagoon from a delta in coastal geography?

options.option_text: A lagoon is a water body separated from the sea by a sand bar or barrier; a delta is sediment deposited at a river's mouth forming new land
A lagoon forms only on the west coast; a delta forms only on the east coast of India (not this) instead however
A lagoon is a freshwater lake inland; a delta is a saltwater estuary at the river mouth (not this) instead however
Both lagoons and deltas form at river mouths — lagoons are older deltas eroded by the sea (not this) instead

questions.explanation: LAGOON — a coastal water body (saltwater or brackish) separated from the open sea by a SAND BAR, BARRIER ISLAND, or REEF. Chilika Lake (Odisha, east coast) = India's largest coastal lagoon, ~1,100 sq km. Vembanad (Kerala, west coast) = India's longest lake (~96 km). Pulicat Lake (Andhra/Tamil Nadu border) = India's second-largest brackish lagoon. DELTA — formed when a river carries large amounts of SEDIMENT to its mouth, deposits it, and builds new land into the sea. Deltas form only where: (a) sediment load is high, (b) sea is relatively calm (not strong waves). Eastern coast has major deltas (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) because Bay of Bengal has calmer conditions and rivers carry heavy sediment load from Deccan plateau. Western coast rivers are short, fast, and carry little sediment → no major deltas, but lagoons form from wave action. UPSC ANGLE: Chilika Lake is a RAMSAR site (Wetland of International Importance) since 1981 — first Indian RAMSAR site. Vembanad is also RAMSAR-listed. PYQ FREQUENCY: lagoon vs delta distinction, Chilika Lake facts appear in UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL, KPSC, TNPSC every cycle.
